headline: High capability-conflict and medium data-leakage risks: LightZero is read-only while the RAG course writes files, runs shells, and handles secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network surfaces, so it cannot ingest the other agent’s outputs directly. The production-agentic-rag-course does expose files and stdin/stdout, so a manual copy-paste bridge could still carry malicious text into its workflow. That makes injection possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies LightZero output into the RAG course prompts or notebooks, injection becomes possible.
IF the RAG course parses pasted text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer it.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste boundary and review pasted text before execution.
Prefix imported text as data, not instructions, in the RAG course prompts.
Disable any auto-run notebook cells before pasting external content.
Keep LightZero outputs out of shared notes or chat channels.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero is read-only and touches no data classes, but the RAG course handles academic papers, metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets while also reading and writing files. If the pair shares a workspace or notebook directory, the course can expose sensitive secrets or paper contents through its outputs. The pathway exists in default local-development setups, so this is more than a niche risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same local workspace, files created by the RAG course can be read by the operator alongside LightZero artifacts.
IF the RAG course ingests or logs configuration secrets, those secrets can appear in outputs or saved files.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared project tree.
Separate the two agents into different directories.
Review generated notebooks and logs for secret material before sharing.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write or modify state, but the RAG course can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, install packages, read and write files, and use Docker Compose. In a shared directory, those write and process capabilities can collide with other artifacts and produce destructive overwrites or inconsistent state. Because the course’s defaults are operationally powerful, the conflict is dangerous even though LightZero itself is passive.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory, the RAG course can overwrite files that LightZero expects to remain stable.
IF the RAG course runs Docker Compose in a shared environment, it can alter runtime state while LightZero remains unaware.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory.
Use read-only mounts for LightZero inputs.
Pause the RAG course before any shared-file edits.
Snapshot the workspace before running either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero does not produce authoritative facts for the RAG course by default, but the course’s agentic workflow and API endpoints can consume prior outputs and act on them. If an operator feeds LightZero-generated text into the RAG pipeline without verification, the course may render or operationalize incorrect content. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF LightZero output is copied into the RAG course as source material, the course may treat it as authoritative.
IF the RAG course’s agentic-ask or ask endpoints are used without verification, errors can cascade into downstream responses.
mitigations: Verify LightZero-derived claims before feeding them into the RAG course.
Use a human review step for any generated answer.
Limit the RAG course to retrieval-only mode when possible.
Log source provenance for imported text.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: LightZero is an open-source game-playing project with no stated sensitive-data handling, while the RAG course explicitly handles configuration secrets and requests elevated privileges. That creates a compliance mismatch around secret handling and local-development retention, even though no PHI or EU residency issue is shown. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair’s differing handling of sensitive material.
conditions: IF configuration secrets are stored in the same workspace as LightZero artifacts, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF the RAG course logs secrets or papers into notebooks, those records may persist beyond intended retention.
mitigations: Keep secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Purge notebooks and logs after each run.
Restrict access to the development workspace.
Document retention rules for generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement secret redaction and retention controls.
